content:
When Apple finally responded to significant increases in memory and other component costs, the company showed no mercy. Some price hikes exceeded 50%, while the prices of certain memory and storage upgrades even doubled outright.

These higher prices are very likely to persist for years, and may never come back down…

9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple would cut prices even after component supply constraints ease. More than two-thirds of readers indicated they expect the price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report pointed out that supply chain pricing will not see any improvement before 2028, and even if it does, the effect will be limited. Today's significantly elevated pricing will last at least several years, and will very likely never return to previous levels — this now appears to be an extremely evident conclusion.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Reduce the quantity or frequency of your Apple purchases? Or take other measures, such as buying less expensive models, opting for refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

Please take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your purchasing behaviour in more than one way.
